data.long_meaning: The name Winfred is derived from the Old English words 'wynn' meaning friend and 'fred' meaning peace. Winfred is a name that signifies a friend who brings peace or harmony. The name Winfred carries the meaning “Friend of peace” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Winfred usually hope their child will grow to embody friend of peace and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew 'wintaradh', meaning 'grace, friend'. In Old Testament usage, it is found in the names of men Wintharoth, Hethloth, and Winthar, meaning 'man of grace'. In biblical usage, it is often used as a term for God's grace and mercy.

in_greek.name: Γυναικειοδότης
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek 'gyneikodotes', meaning 'woman-giver'. In biblical Greek, it is used in the New Testament to refer to God as the giver of women, and by extension, the giver of all good things.

in_latin.name: Venantia
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin 'venantia', meaning 'coming, bringing'. In biblical Latin, it is used in the Vulgate to refer to God as the one who comes to save, and by extension, to the concept of divine grace.

in_english.name: Winfred
in_english.meaning: Friend of man, fair-haired, wolf strength
in_english.long_meaning: From the Old English 'Wynn-frið', meaning 'friend of man'. The Old English 'wynn' means 'joy, friendship', and 'frið' means 'peace, friend'. In English usage, it is often associated with the idea of a fair-haired warrior or a friend who brings strength and victory.
